subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs, deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs, deployment topology

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap of what we heard and the recommended next steps so the team has a single source of truth. Please reply with any edits or gaps.

Summary of pain / goals
- Critical: reduce input-to-response latency for customer-facing chat (payments support flows) while keeping unit cost under control.
- Target SLOs you described: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 450ms for generation up to ~256 tokens; tail latency is the biggest customer impact right now.
- Throughput: steady-state ~150 req/s for US-east, with burst capacity up to ~500 req/s during peak daily windows.
- Security/regulatory: all PCI-adjacent data must stay within your VPC for full auditability; audit logs and KMS integration required.
- Model: two-model pipeline — a lightweight re-ranker (~3B) for candidate scoring and a larger generator (~13B) for final responses.

Key technical notes & recommended topology
- Deployment mode: Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) in your us-east VPC for production. Private control plane with customer-managed networking to meet audit requirements.
- Hardware & model hosting: recommend H100-class instances for the 13B generator in int8/4-bit quantized form, A100/RTX6000-class for the re-ranker depending on your latency testing.
- Autoscaling & burst: reserve baseline capacity to meet steady-state throughput and configure burst pools for traffic spikes (we can automate fallback to smaller model variants if capacity is saturated).
- Batching & caching: use continuous batching with a low-latency window (5-10ms) and prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts. This should materially reduce p95 for common queries.
- Kernel selection & sequence length: tune kernels for typical 128–256 token generation to avoid unnecessary memory/compute overhead.
- Observability: token-level latency traces, per-route dashboards, and regression alerts tied to your evaluation prompts (we'll onboard your prompt set).

Open questions we agreed to follow up on
1) Exact token/response size distribution for your most common flows (can you share a sample histogram?).
2) Acceptable cold-start latency for transient instances (do you need <1s warm-up for burst nodes?).
3) Any hard requirement on model provenance (need for vetted models only vs. custom fine-tuned weights?).

Attachments & references
- Attached: acme-map-requirements.xlsx (your sheet), acme-infra-diagram.png (notes from call)
- Internal: INF-452 (capacity planning ticket) — link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-452

Next steps / proposed timeline
- Redwood to produce a Dedicated proposal (capacity + pricing) and a baseline topology within 3 business days — attaching the initial draft.
- Schedule 60-min technical kickoff (includes your infra, security, and platform teams) — propose Wed/Thu next week; please confirm availability.
- Sandbox test: we'll provide a private sandbox with a representative model to run a throughput/latency sweep and share results.

Thanks — looping in Dev and Neha for the sizing and Marcus for the deployment plan.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks Marissa — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications: 

- On the p95 <= 450ms target: is that realistic for a quantized 13B model on H100 hardware for 256-token outputs? We want to make sure expectations are aligned before we share SLOs internally.
- For throughput, our merchants expect <200ms median during peak times; how does that map to the p50 you listed?
- We attached a slightly expanded requirements sheet (acme-map-requirements.xlsx) with traffic windows and token distributions.

Would also like a high-level cost estimate (monthly committed capacity) we can show finance before the technical kickoff. Can you include that in the Dedicated proposal?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Jim and I are available Thurs morning ET for the kickoff.

\u0014Sarah

Hi Sarah — quick follow-up from the engineering sizing side. Short answers to the questions you raised and what we'll validate in the sandbox: 

- p95 feasibility: for 13B quantized (int8 / 4-bit) on H100 with continuous batching and prefix cache, a p95 ~350–450ms for 128–256 token responses is realistic in our benchmarks. We achieve lower tails when cache hits are high. We'll run an end-to-end sweep in the sandbox to produce a P50/P95/P99 distribution.
- p50 vs median: p50 is the median — the 120ms figure maps to fast-path/cached responses; uncached generations will be higher.
- Hardware recommendation: baseline cluster of 4 x H100-80GB for generator (handles steady 150 req/s with room for autoscale). Add 2 x A100-40GB for the re-ranker and as warm standby. We'll provide a costed Dedicated proposal with those configurations.
- Quantization & model variants: recommend internal A/B where generator runs int8 quantized for latency-sensitive paths and a higher-precision variant is available for quality-sensitive flows. Auto-fallback policies can route to higher-precision models on demand.
- Networking & VPC: we'll use Private deployment with VPC peering; KMS integration for key management and audit logs forwarded to your SIEM.

Attached: redwood-dedicated-proposal.pdf (initial capacity + pricing estimate). We'll confirm exact instance SKUs and pricing in the final doc.

Proposed next step: Technical kickoff Thursday 10:00 AM ET — agenda: (1) infra & networking requirements, (2) model hosting & quantization plan, (3) sandbox validation plan and metrics.

Marissa / Sarah — if that time works, we'll send a calendar invite and include our infra ops lead.

Thanks,
